ch.intro: Pick one channel for your phone: Bark on iPhone, ntfy on Android. Email is a record, not an alarm.
ch.sent_unverified: Sent, not yet confirmed by ntfy
ch.desc.ntfy: Works on Android and iPhone. On iPhone it shows ntfy's own icon.
ch.desc.bark: Shows the OhmyTesla icon. Alarms ring even in silent mode.
ch.desc.telegram: Messages from your own bot, with a clip thumbnail when available.
ch.desc.email: Slow (minutes). Use it as a record, not your only alarm channel.
ch.desc.webhook: POSTs JSON to a URL — for Home Assistant, Node-RED or your own scripts.
ch.desc.apprise: Any of the 100+ services Apprise supports (Pushover, Discord, Slack…). Separate URLs with commas.
ch.bark_s1: Install Bark from the App Store and allow notifications.
ch.bark_s2: Copy the address shown in Bark (https://api.day.app/…).
ch.bark_s3: Paste it here, save, then Send test.
ch.problem.missing_token: Needs access token and chat ID
ch.ntfy_new_hint: On a public server the topic name is the password.
ch.ntfy_created: Private topic created. Subscribe to it in the ntfy app.
ch.ntfy_scan: In the ntfy app, tap + and subscribe to this topic, or scan: {url}
fleet.heading: Vehicle controls
fleet.intro: Teslas built since 2021, Cybertruck included, only accept commands signed by a key they've approved. TeslaMate's sign-in can read data but can't sign. These steps give this hub its own key, approved by you, so commands go straight to your vehicle with no third party. One-time setup, about 10 minutes.
fleet.sum_pair: Approve the key in the Tesla app
fleet.s1_hint: The private key never leaves this machine. You publish only the public key.
fleet.s2: Register a free Tesla developer app
fleet.s2_hint: At developer.tesla.com, create a Fleet API app. Allowed origin: https://<your domain>. Redirect URI: {redirect}. Grant types: authorization code and client credentials. Scopes: vehicle information, location, commands, charging. Tesla's monthly credit covers one personal vehicle, but set a billing limit above $0. Then enter the app details here.
fleet.s3_hint: Tesla checks that your domain serves the key at {url}. Easiest: a free GitHub Pages site, <you>.github.io, with the downloaded file at that path and an empty .nojekyll file. Then check and register.
fleet.s4: Sign in with your Tesla account
fleet.s4_hint: Approve the permissions on Tesla's page; you'll return here automatically. If the page you land on doesn't load, paste its full address below.
fleet.paste_ph: …or paste the address you landed on
fleet.s5_hint: On the phone with the Tesla app, scan the code or open the link, then approve. The vehicle must be online and will ask you to confirm.
fleet.pair_scan: Scan with the phone that has the Tesla app.
fleet.s6_hint: Commands now go from this hub to your vehicle, signed with your key. Starting over keeps the key; no need to approve it again.
fleet.reset_lead: Clears the developer app details and sign-in. The key is kept, so the vehicle's approval stays valid.
sentrycfg.heading: Sentry alerts
sentrycfg.intro: How to tell you about activity around the parked vehicle. An alarm (alarm sounding, opened while locked, vehicle moved) always pushes. Activity means someone came close.
sentrycfg.home_none: Not set: activity in your driveway counts as “Everywhere else”.
sentrycfg.at_home_desc: You walk past it all day.
sentrycfg.fast_desc: How often to check while Sentry Mode is on (otherwise every 60 s). Free, no extra battery.
sentrycfg.fleet_note: For instant (1–3 s) alerts, including door-handle pulls with Sentry off, connect Fleet Telemetry (see docs/FLEET-TELEMETRY.md).
models.heading: 3D models
models.intro: The vehicle on the Overview page. Upload your own .glb per model; nodes named door_fl, frunk, tailgate, tonneau… open and close with the real vehicle. See static/models/README.md.
